title: Plane-stress isotropic free thermal expansion
purpose: Verify the sign, reference temperature, plane-stress reduction, and operator placement of the equivalent thermal-expansion load.
physics: small-strain isotropic plane-stress thermoelasticity under uniform temperature change

execution.evidence: A minimally restrained unit-length plate heated uniformly by 100 K must expand by alpha times 100 in the free x direction.

observables: The x displacement of every node on the right edge is alpha DeltaT L.
The thermoelastic property record exposes rho cp and reference temperature.
The Arrhenius creep multiplier increases above its reference temperature and decreases below it.
acceptance: The right-edge displacement matches the analytical free-expansion value within the automated tolerance.
The material rejects nonpositive conductivity, heat capacity, or absolute reference temperature.
limitations: The benchmark does not validate a monolithic fully coupled temperature-displacement solve.
Temperature-dependent elastic and thermal property tables are not covered.
